intro.text:
TERRAN ASCENDANCY MANDATE - Exoplanetary Forces. Neural Training Facility, Bay 3.

You are a recruit. Before any landing or boarding, the Mandate teaches your nerves what a unit sees: situation awareness, close-quarters tactics, how to stay alive in a corridor.

An instructor bot seats you in a rugged simulator pod and checks the straps twice. As you lock your helmet to the connector, you notice the staff - too many of them, moving too fast. Half the pods in your row are dark. Two have their panels off; one is held shut with tape and a cable tie.

Your simconnector buzzes. The first battle simulatron begins.

SCENARIO: a facility built round one machine, meant to run as root forever. Something answered from below the hardware, and the machine's daemons became something else. Every human account was revoked at once. Yours too.

You are rootless. Every door checks permissions you no longer have.

e1_end.text:
The exit switch takes your weight and the lift drops into the dark.

Somewhere below, a clock is ticking that was not ticking before. Cron got away. It does not chase, it schedules - and it has put you on its list.

For a moment the sim thins out: the inside of the pod's lid, a red light, someone shouting a number that might be yours. Then the dark comes back.

The lift stops with a bang at a loading dock. Containers to the roof, and something big and yellow parked in a bay.

outro_demo.text:
SIMULATION PAUSED. End of the demo - Episode 1 goes on in the full game.

Free programs of the simulatron, made new each run: --level sim1 (Long Fens, open land without end), sim2 (Deep Swap, floor after floor) and sim3 (Swap Sprawl, rooms without end); and training programs: sim4 (Kill House: squads), sim5 (Bus Run, side on, in real time) and sim6 (Purge, from above, in real time) sim7 (Xantrium Rush, real-time strategy), sim8 (Fen Hopper, flight) sim9 (Coolant Loop, a reactor's systems), sim10 (Root Shell, card duels) and sim11 (Deep Works: magboots, stairs, a jetpack, the water and a submarine).

outro_lose.text:
SIMULATION FAILED. Process terminated.

The pod hisses and the lid stays shut. "Again," says the instructor bot. Read the tells, use the barrels, step off the marked floor.

e1m9_intro.text:
Behind the goggles' closet, a switch nobody labelled. You throw it anyway. The floor drops: a service lift, old and loud, going down past the boot bay into the swap partition.

This part of the simulatron was not in the briefing.

e1m9_end.text:
The last page is swapped back in. Somewhere above, Cron's schedule skips a beat - it knows a process got out of its queue.

The instructor bot cuts in, too loud and too late: "Recruit, that sector is not part of your training. Do not disconnect." A lift takes you up through the dark, and lets you out at a loading dock.

e1m2_end.text:
The control room's switch drops the dock's gantry. Every container in that bay held a library something needs; the loader links each one to where it runs. You have just been linked too - into whatever runs beneath the hardware.

The instructor bot's voice comes through broken: "...pod six... pod six is not answering..." Your pod is six.

The gantry's lift drops you one floor down, into a hall that smells of hot metal and ozone. Something is being built here.

e1m3_end.text:
The hopper sinks into the warm swamp up to its fan pods. Out here the sim runs thin: the horizon flickers like a bad cable, and the planet over the ridges has a seam down its middle.

Then the sky tears along that seam, and for a moment you see the inside of a pod's lid again - lit red - and hands on the release. "Not yet," somebody says. "He is still in there." The dark comes back.

It lifts on a wider swamp. Fens to the horizon, lakes that smell of Xantrium, and far to the north-east a red light blinking on a mast.

e1m4_end.text:
The switch drops. The mast's lamp stops blinking and burns steady, and the fens go quiet - the drones settle where they hover, the water stops moving, the sky holds still like a picture.

"Relay reached," says the instructor bot, too calm. "Evaluation complete. Uplink to User Space in three." Two. Nobody counts the one.

Next: User Space.

sim1_end.text:
The relay's switch drops and the program stops where it is: the fens hold still to every horizon. Somewhere past the last hill, the simulatron has already stopped drawing them.

"Free program complete," says the instructor bot. "Run it again and it will be another place."

sim2_down.text: You drop through the exit. Under you the next floor is being written as you fall: rooms first, then corridors, then what waits in them.

sim3_end.text: The exit takes you out of the sprawl. Behind you its rooms go on, made only when someone walks into them - and nobody will.

sim4_end.text: UNIT EVALUATION: squad tactics. The instructor bot's voice is flat: "Packs, sweeps, ambushes, assaults. Out there they will not be a program."

sim5_end.text: UNIT EVALUATION: movement. "Sixteen chips and the bus is yours," says the instructor bot. "Out there the floor will not wait for you to jump."

sim6_end.text: UNIT EVALUATION: sector purge. The last sentry goes dark and the map fades to its grid. "Clean," says the instructor bot. "Now do it without seeing it from above."

sim7_end.text: UNIT EVALUATION: command. The last kernel node folds into the grid and the swamp goes quiet. "You think in squads now," says the instructor bot. "The real Xantrium fields will not hold still for you."

sim8_end.text: UNIT EVALUATION: flight. The hopper settles on the far pad and the fens fade to grid. "Soft enough," says the instructor bot. "The real hopper has a crew compartment. Remember that."

sim9_end.text: UNIT EVALUATION: systems. The shift log closes in the green. "The facility ran on a loop like that once," says the instructor bot, and does not say what happened to it.

sim10_end.text: UNIT EVALUATION: intrusion. "You did not need the gun," says the instructor bot. "In the real root, you will not have one."

sim11_end.text: UNIT EVALUATION: mobility. "Boots, stairs, a jetpack, a submarine," says the instructor bot. "The real station has all of them. It also has what flooded it."

e1m5_end.text:
The lift drops through the floor of user space and does not slow down. The numbers on its panel count rings, not decks: 3, 2, 1.

At ring 0 the doors open on a hall that hums like a held breath. Somewhere in it a crontab is ticking - your crontab - and every line of it has your name.

Next: Kernel Space.
